subject: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency commitment & fallback plan - post-demo clarifications
messages:
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Park <simon@fastlane.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-12-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated: clarifying latency/throughput targets after demo

Hi Simon / Elena —

Thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can recommend the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC). We want to ensure our recommendation matches your latency and throughput constraints and the operational constraints you mentioned.

Recap from our side:
- Workload: query expansion + shopping-cart personalization at inference time (model: 13B transformer, quantized).
- Traffic profile: peak shopping hours (10–12 PST), baseline 20 qps, peak bursts to 250 qps for ~10-minute spikes.
- Latency target: 50–75 ms p50 for simple prompts; 150–200 ms p95 for heavy prompts.
- Data/safety: no PII, but regionally restricted content for EU customers (you did mention some EU-only traffic).

Asks: please confirm the following so we can finalize a recommended pilot plan: 1) Are the peak/steady QPS numbers above accurate? 2) Can you tolerate up to ~200 ms p95 during sustained peak periods, or do you need tighter guarantees? 3) Any corporate procurement or network constraints that require private VPC/on-prem?

Attached: preliminary SLO runbook and suggested pilot MOP (pilot_mop.xlsx). If you confirm the numbers, we'll propose a short pilot and a dedicated sizing estimate (if Dedicated is the move) and a Hosted fallback plan to cover burst windows.

Next step: if you confirm today, I'll loop in our Capacity team and surface a rough cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated for the pilot.

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Simon Park <simon@fastlane.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@fastlane.ai>
Date: 2028-12-05T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated: clarifying latency/throughput targets after demo

Jonas —

Thanks for the recap. Numbers broadly match our telemetry. A few clarifications:
- Baseline is actually closer to 28 qps (I rounded down on the call).
- Peak bursts: 220–280 qps across the US region, typically lasting 6–12 minutes.
- Latency: we require p50 <= 60 ms, p95 ideally <= 175 ms during normal peaks. For promotional events we can tolerate up to 250 ms p95 but prefer not to.
- Procurement: we can start with Hosted for speed, but procurement/legal is pushing for Dedicated once we move past pilot (data residency + contractual SLAs). No immediate VPC/on-prem requirement.

Happy to take your sizing and cost delta. Can you include expected failover behavior (if Dedicated hit capacity) and estimated cold-start implications if we scale down overnight?

Simon
Simon Park
Head of ML Engineering
FastLane Retail

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-12-05T12:10:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: quick recommendation for FastLane (hosted + staged Dedicated)

Team —

Quick internal note based on Simon's confirm: baseline ~28 qps, peaks ~220–280 qps, p50 <= 60 ms, p95 target <= 175 ms. They can accept up to 250 ms for promo spikes. No immediate VPC requirement, but procurement will push for Dedicated after pilot.

Recommendation (short):
- Pilot on Hosted API with dedicated reserved lanes (burst reservation) for promo windows. This gets them fast time-to-value and lets procurement evaluate contracts in parallel.
- Parallel capacity-sizing exercise for Dedicated: target pool sized to handle 300 qps sustained (buffer for model variance), with autoscale and cross-region fallback.
- Fallback behavior: Hosted fallback + automatic routing to a lower-cost quantized variant if Dedicated hit limits. Document trade-offs in SLO runbook.

I'll draft a short note for Simon describing the pilot runway, cost delta, and SLA expectations. Marissa, can you add rough Dedicated GPU counts for a 300 qps sizing?

-ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Park <simon@fastlane.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-12-05T15:47:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted pilot proposal + Dedicated sizing next steps

Simon / Elena —

Thanks for confirming numbers. Based on your telemetry and Ben's quick sizing note, here's the proposed path and immediate asks: 

Proposed path:
1) 6-week Hosted pilot (fast onboarding) with:
   - Reserved burst lanes for promo windows (auto-burst to additional hosted capacity).
   - Instrumentation & tracing: per-route latency and token-level cost in the console.
   - Runbook: we'll lock p50/p95 targets and collect a 2-week telemetry baseline for Dedicated sizing.
2) Parallel Dedicated sizing exercise (8 business days) to model a 300 qps steady-state target with headroom for autoscale; deliverable will include GPU counts, expected cost delta, and fallback policy.
3) Procurement packet: draft terms and SLA options for Dedicated; we'll give a first pass in 10 business days.

Immediate asks from FastLane:
- Sign the pilot SoW (I attached pilot_mop.xlsx) and confirm three representative traffic windows for telemetry.
- Approve Redwood access to anonymized telemetry for sizing (read-only).

Fallbacks and failover behavior:
- If Dedicated reaches capacity during ramp, traffic will failover to Hosted (same model family) with an automated throttling policy; the console will show routing changes and latency shifts.
- For cost-sensitive windows we can roll a lower-precision quantized variant; we'll flag any measurable quality regressions in the trial.

I'll send a formal pilot SoW and a short one-page comparison (Hosted vs Dedicated) with cost ballpark later today. If you can confirm the pilot signoff by EOD Wednesday, we can target onboarding next Monday.

Best —
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
